device_info: CPU (Ryzen 9 9900X, WSL2), Backend::Vector (training) / Optimized (lens), f32 compute, BF16 weights
note: Book 3, step 3: the student learns the teacher's replies (spec/measurements/teacher-qwen36-capitals.json: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, all 47 right, each reply the capital alone) instead of the hand-written stand-ins of cpu-prefecture-capitals-replay.json, for the same 8 trained and 14 replay prefectures (examples/prefecture-capitals-teacher-train.jsonl, -teacher-train-replay.jsonl, the whole reply scored). Compared with the untrained student by tools/compare_capitals.py on examples/prefecture-capitals-split-replay.json; the hand-written runs of the same settings are in cpu-prefecture-capitals-replay.json. Result: the teacher's form is learned, and with replay so is the shortcut. Free answers become the bare city, as the teacher writes them. The 14 replay pairs are all same-name prefectures (青森県 -> 青森市), so 14 of the 22 examples fit the rule 'prefecture name + 市', and at full FFN lr 1e-6 x 100 the student answers that way for the different-name prefectures too (茨城市, 栃木市, 群馬市, 愛知市): among the 18 different-name prefectures (東京都 aside) the free answer contains the shortcut 9 times untrained, 3 times with the hand-written replay run, 10 times with the teacher replay run (1 with the teacher pairs and no replay). The same-name guards then look protected (free 14/14) for the wrong reason, which the forced position cannot tell apart (the correct and shortcut first tokens are the same). The trained capitals do worse than with the hand-written frame: full FFN lr 1e-6 x 100 free right 7 -> 4 of 8 without replay, 6 -> 2 with it; at lr 3e-6 x 100 with replay 8/8 free right but the guards still collapse to trained cities (free 9/14). LoRA 8 lr 1e-4 x 30 with the teacher's replies is under-trained (0/8). README KL is about twice the hand-written runs' (0.013-0.034), as the bare form departs further from the student's own. Conclusion for the design: the replay set must not be all same-name, or it teaches the shortcut; the different-name guards (3) and the shortcut count are the measures to trust. Free answers are cut at 16 tokens.
